title: Huevos Rancheros
subtitle: fried eggs on corn tortillas with tomato and chilli sauce
excerpt: Huevos rancheros is a quick Mexican breakfast of fried eggs served on warm corn tortillas, covered in a simple tomato and jalapeño sauce. It comes together in about 30 minutes. Refried beans and sliced avocado alongside are optional but good.
sourceNotes: Huevos rancheros, meaning ranch-style eggs, began as a mid-morning meal for Mexican farmworkers. The dish spread across the country and became a breakfast staple throughout Mexico and the American Southwest.

content.text: This recipe serves 2 and takes 30 minutes from start to plate. The tomato sauce takes about 15 minutes to cook while you warm the tortillas and fry the eggs. Everything comes together quickly, so have all the components ready before you start frying.

Use a wide frying pan with a lid when cooking the eggs. Covering the pan for the last minute of cooking sets the whites firmly without flipping the eggs, so the yolks stay runny. If you prefer fully set yolks, simply leave the lid on a minute longer.

Make the sauce. Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it is soft and translucent. Add the garlic and jalapeño and cook for 1 more minute.

Pour in the crushed tomatoes. Season with salt. Bring to a simmer and cook over medium-low heat for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has thickened and the raw tomato taste has gone. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Keep warm on a low heat.

Warm the tortillas. Heat a dry frying pan over medium-high heat and warm each tortilla for about 30 seconds per side until hot and slightly charred at the edges. Stack them and cover with a clean cloth to keep warm.

Fry the eggs. Heat the remaining tablespoon of oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Crack all four eggs in, spacing them apart. Season with salt. Cover the pan with a lid and cook for 2 minutes until the whites are set but the yolks are still soft. Remove the lid and check.

To serve, lay 2 warmed tortillas on each plate, overlapping slightly. Spoon a generous amount of tomato sauce over the tortillas. Slide 2 fried eggs on top. Spoon a little more sauce around the eggs. Scatter over the chopped coriander. Serve with optional sliced avocado and refried beans on the side.

attrs.symptom: The egg whites are cooked but the yolks are fully set.
attrs.cause: The pan was too hot or the lid was left on too long.
attrs.fix: Use medium rather than medium-high heat and check after 90 seconds. Remove the lid the moment the whites are just set.

attrs.symptom: The tortillas have gone chewy and cold before serving.
attrs.cause: They were warmed too far in advance.
attrs.fix: Warm the tortillas last, just before serving, and keep them covered in a clean cloth until needed.

attrs.symptom: The sauce is too thin and runs off the tortillas.
attrs.cause: It was not reduced for long enough.
attrs.fix: Turn up the heat and cook the sauce for a further 5 minutes, stirring often, until it holds its shape on a spoon.

content.text: Huevos rancheros started on working farms in rural Mexico as a late-morning meal. It spread into homes and cafes across the country. The dish is popular throughout Mexico and in the American Southwest. It is one of the simplest Mexican breakfasts to cook at home and needs almost no special ingredients.
